questions.question: Define web hosting, and why is it necessary for websites?
questions.solution_html:
• Definition
  • Web hosting is a service that allows individuals and organizations to store website files on a server
  • connected to the internet, making the website accessible to users worldwide.
  • Why Web Hosting is Necessary
  • • Online Storage: Website files (HTML, CSS, images, databases) need to be stored on a server that
  • is always online.
  • • 24/7 Accessibility: Hosting ensures users can visit the website at any time from anywhere in the
  • world.
  • • Domain Linking: Web hosting allows a domain name (e.g., www.example.com) to be linked to
  • the website through DNS.
  • • Security: Hosting providers offer SSL certificates, firewalls, and malware protection.
  • • Email Hosting: Business email accounts linked to the domain are also provided.
  • Types of Web Hosting
  • • Shared Hosting – Multiple websites on one server
  • • VPS Hosting – Dedicated virtual resources
  • • Dedicated Hosting – Entire server for one website
  • • Cloud Hosting – Resources spread across multiple servers

questions.question: List and briefly explain the advantages of using AJAX in web / applications.
questions.solution_html:
• List and briefly explain the advantages of using AJAX in web applications.
  • What is AJAX?
  • AJAX (Asynchronous JavaScript and XML) is a technique that allows web pages to communicate
  • with a server and update content without reloading the entire page.
  • Advantages
  • • Asynchronous Communication: Data is sent and received in the background without interrupting
  • the user's interaction with the page.
  • • Reduced Server Load: Only the required data is fetched instead of reloading the entire page
  • reducing bandwidth and server usage.
  • • Faster User Experience: The page feels faster because only parts of it are updated, not the whole
  • page.
  • • Improved Interactivity: Features like live search suggestions, auto-complete, and real-time
  • updates are possible.
  • • Platform Independence: Works with any server-side language (PHP, Python, Java) and any
  • modern browser.
  • • Partial Page Update: Only specific sections are updated, preserving the rest of the page layout.
  • Mark Allocation
  • Definition of AJAX (1 Mark)
  • Any 4 advantages clearly explained (4 Marks)

  • • Purpose: Used for sending email messages.
  • • Port: 25 (or 465/587 for secure connections)
  • • Working: The mail client sends the email to the SMTP server, which routes it to the recipient's
  • mail server.

questions.question: Describe the key features of AJAX-based web applications with / examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction
  • AJAX-based web applications are dynamic applications that update content by communicating with a
  • server asynchronously using the XMLHttpRequest object or the Fetch API, without a full page reload.
  • Key Features
  • • Asynchronous Data Loading: Data loads in the background while the user continues to interact.
  • Example: Gmail loads new emails without refreshing the page.
  • • Partial Page Updates: Only a specific part of the page is updated. Example: Facebook's newsfeed
  • adds new posts without a full reload.
  • • Real-Time Data: Applications can fetch live data. Example: Stock price dashboards, live sports
  • scores.
  • • Reduced Bandwidth: Only JSON or XML data is transferred, not full HTML pages. Example
  • Google Maps loads map tiles incrementally.
  • • Better User Experience: Smooth transitions, live form validations, and dynamic content.
  • Example: Checking username availability while signing up.
  • • Cross-Platform Support: Works across browsers and different server-side technologies.
  • Page 3
  • Basic AJAX Example
  • const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
  • xhr.open('GET', 'data.php', true);
  • xhr.onload = function() {
  • if (xhr.status === 200) {
  • document.getElementById('result').innerHTML = xhr.responseText;
  • }
  • };
  • xhr.send();
  • Mark Allocation
  • Any 3 features with examples (3 Marks)
  • Code example showing AJAX call (2 Marks)
  • POP3 – Post Office Protocol version 3
  • • Purpose: Used to retrieve emails from the server to a local client.
  • • Port: 110
  • • Working: Downloads emails to the local device and (by default) deletes them from the server.
  • • Limitation: Emails are stored locally and are not accessible from multiple devices.
  • slice(start, end)
  • Extracts part of a string from start index to end index (end not included). Supports negative indices.
  • let str = 'Web Technologies';
  • console.log(str.slice(0, 3)); // Web
  • console.log(str.slice(-12)); // Technologies

questions.question: Describe the purpose and working of different web protocols.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction
  • A web protocol is a set of rules that defines how data is transmitted and received over the internet.
  • Protocols ensure reliable communication between different devices and systems.
  • DNS – Domain Name System
  • • Purpose: Translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
  • • Port: 53
  • • Working: When you type www.google.com, a DNS query is sent to a DNS resolver, which finds
  • the corresponding IP address (e.g., 142.250.195.46) and returns it to the browser.
  • • Common DNS Records: A (IPv4 address), AAAA (IPv6), MX (mail server), CNAME (alias).
  • replace() and replaceAll()
  • replace() replaces the first occurrence of a substring. replaceAll() replaces all occurrences.
  • let str = 'Hello World';
  • console.log(str.replace('World', 'MGU')); // Hello MGU
  • let s = 'aabbaa';
  • console.log(s.replaceAll('a', 'x')); // xxbbxx
